text: Pachavita is a town and municipality located in the Neira Province of the Colombian department of Boyacá. Its urban center lies on the Altiplano Cundiboyacense at an altitude of 1,985 metres (6,512 ft), approximately 85 kilometres (53 mi) from Tunja, the departmental capital. The municipality shares borders with Chinavita to the north, Tenza and La Capilla to the south, Garagoa to the east, and Úmbita to the west. The name Pachavita originates from the Chibcha language, where "pacha" means man or lord and "vita" means point, summit, or peak, translating to "Peak of the man"; alternatively, it is interpreted as "Proud chief." Prior to the Spanish conquistadors' arrival, the region belonged to the Muisca Confederation, under the rule of the zaque of Hunza. Modern Pachavita was officially founded on November 17, 1716. The primary economic activities in the area are agriculture and dairy farming, producing yuca, maize, bananas, arracacha, beans, lulo, cucumbers, eggs, peas, and cheese.
